Business context & process design

How the procurement module models real-world purchasing operations — lifecycle, roles, controls, and financial safeguards.

Procurement Lifecycle

The procurement cycle follows a structured purchase-to-pay (P2P) process designed to ensure organisational spend is authorised, competitive, and accurately recorded in the books.

📋

Sourcing

  • Supplier onboarding
  • Request for Quotation
  • Quotation evaluation
  • Contract negotiation
→
🛒

Ordering

  • Purchase Requisition
  • Internal approval
  • Purchase Order issuance
  • Supplier acknowledgement
→
📦

Receiving

  • Goods Receipt Note
  • Quality inspection
  • Partial delivery handling
  • Returns processing
→
💳

Financials

  • Supplier invoice receipt
  • Three-way matching
  • Bill approval
  • Payment authorisation

Why this structure matters

Each stage creates a documented audit trail. The three-way match at the bill stage ensures the organisation only pays for goods that were actually ordered (PO) and received (GRN) at the agreed price — protecting against fraud, billing errors, and overpayment.

Roles & Responsibilities

👤

Requester

Any staff member who identifies a need. Creates purchase requisitions and tracks their status. Cannot approve their own requests.

Permissions: ec_purchase_requisitions.view, ec_purchase_requisitions.create

✅

Approver

Manager or delegated authority who reviews and approves or rejects procurement documents. Receives notifications for pending items in their inbox.

Acts via: Approval Engine inbox or direct approval link in notification email.

🏢

Procurement Officer

Manages the sourcing cycle end-to-end — supplier registration, RFQs, PO creation and confirmation, contract management.

Permissions: ec_suppliers.*, ec_purchase_orders.*, ec_rfqs.*

📦

Warehouse / Receiver

Records physical delivery of goods and posts Goods Receipt Notes. Responsible for quality inspection and returns initiation.

Permissions: ec_goods_receipts.*, ec_purchase_returns.*

💰

Finance Officer

Processes supplier invoices as purchase bills, reviews three-way match results, and approves or escalates discrepancies.

Permissions: ec_purchase_bills.*, ec_reports.view

⚙

Procurement Admin

Configures approval workflows, manages system settings, views all reports, and has override capability on discrepancies.

Permissions: all of the above plus ec_approval_workflows.*

Document Statuses

Every procurement document moves through a defined set of statuses. The status controls what actions are available and who can perform them.

Requisitions & Purchase Orders

Draft → Submit → Pending Approval → Approve → Approved / Confirmed → Receive → Partially Received → Fully Received

Rejection at any approval step returns the document to the requester for revision. Cancellation is available before any goods receipt has been posted.

Purchase Bills

Draft → Pending Approval → Approved → Paid

Purchase Returns

Draft → Pending Approval → Approved → Completed

Approval & Escalation

All approval routing is delegated to the Approval Engine — a central, policy-driven service that is independent of any specific business domain. This means procurement approval rules are configured once and applied consistently.

How policies work

Each approval policy targets a combination of Process Type (PROCUREMENT) and Action Code (e.g. REQ_SUBMIT, PO_RELEASE, PURCHASE_BILL_SUBMIT). When a document is submitted:

  1. The Approval Engine evaluates all active policies matching the process type and action code.
  2. It selects the highest-priority matching policy whose condition expression is satisfied by the document's context (e.g. amount, department).
  3. It creates an approval request and notifies the first-step approvers by email and in-app notification.
  4. Each subsequent step is activated only after the previous step is completed.

Escalation

The background worker checks pending approvals every 30 minutes. If an approver has not acted within 24 hours, a reminder notification is sent. There is no automatic escalation to a substitute approver — the Procurement Admin can manually reassign if needed.

Multi-step example: A purchase order over £10,000 might require (1) Line Manager approval, then (2) Finance Controller approval. Both must complete in sequence before the PO is confirmed.

Three-Way Matching

Three-way matching is the financial control that prevents overpayment. It compares three documents at the line level:

🛒
Purchase Order

What was ordered and at what price

⊕
📦
Goods Receipt

What was actually received (accepted quantity)

⊕
🧾
Purchase Bill

What the supplier is charging

=
Match Result

Matched / Partial / Discrepancy

Matching logic

For each bill line, the system finds the corresponding GRN accepted quantity (or falls back to PO ordered quantity). The match value is calculated as: 

matched_value = min(billed_qty, authorised_qty) × unit_price
discrepancy   = max(0, total_bill_amount − matched_value)
  • Matched: discrepancy is zero or within a configured tolerance.
  • Partial match: some lines match but others have differences.
  • Discrepancy: the billed amount meaningfully exceeds what was authorised by the GRN/PO.

A discrepancy does not automatically block a bill — a Finance Officer with the right permission can perform a Direct Approve, attaching a reason for audit purposes.

Contract Management

Contracts formalise long-term supplier relationships and provide a reference framework for purchase orders placed under them. Key business benefits:

  • Locked pricing — POs referencing an active contract auto-apply negotiated rates, preventing price drift.
  • Spend visibility — all POs linked to a contract are aggregated, giving a real-time view of commitment vs. contract value.
  • Automatic alerts — expiry notifications are sent 30 days before a contract ends, ensuring renewals are not missed.
  • Legal record — the legal clauses, governing law, and scope of work are stored and retrievable for dispute resolution.

Contract types

Framework AgreementAn umbrella contract; individual call-off POs are placed under it as needed.
Blanket OrderA fixed-value contract; POs reduce the remaining committed value.
Service AgreementFor ongoing services with a defined scope, SLA, and periodic billing schedule.

Compliance & Audit

Every significant action in the procurement module is recorded in the activity log. This provides a complete, tamper-evident audit trail for internal review, financial audits, and regulatory compliance.

What is logged

  • Document creation, edits, and status changes
  • Approval decisions (approve / reject / reassign) with timestamps and actor identity
  • Three-way match results and any discrepancy overrides with reasons
  • Reminder notifications sent and received
  • Supplier registration and changes
  • Contract sign-off and expiry events

Segregation of duties

The system enforces separation of duties at the application layer:

  • A requester cannot approve their own requisition.
  • A PO creator cannot post a GRN against their own PO (when configured).
  • A bill creator cannot perform a direct-approve on a bill with discrepancy — requires a separate Finance Officer role.

Three-Way Match Algorithm

Implemented in PurchaseBillService.ComputeThreeWayMatch(). Matching is done at the line level by correlating bill items to GRN lines (or PO lines as fallback) using productId first, then normalised description. 

foreach bill_item in bill.Items:
  // 1. Find authorised quantity from GRN (preferred) or PO
  grn_line   = grn.Lines.FirstOrDefault(l => l.ProductId == bill_item.ProductId
                                          || Normalize(l.Description) == Normalize(bill_item.Description))
  po_line    = po.Lines.FirstOrDefault(same match logic)
  authorised_qty = grn_line?.AcceptedQty ?? po_line?.OrderedQty ?? 0
  // 2. Calculate matched value for this line
  line_matched = Min(bill_item.Quantity, authorised_qty) Ã— bill_item.UnitPrice
  matched_total += line_matched
// 3. Compute discrepancy
discrepancy = Max(0, total_bill_amount âˆ’ matched_total)
// 4. Determine status
if   discrepancy == 0                      â†’ "matched"
elif discrepancy < total_bill_amount * 0.1 â†’ "partial_match"   // within 10 %
else                                       â†’ "discrepancy"
The 10 % tolerance threshold is currently hard-coded. It will be made configurable per tenant in a future release.
